A Pakistani activist for girls' education, born in 1997 in Mingora in the Swat valley. A gunman of the Pakistani Taliban shot her in the head in 2012; she survived, and in 2014, at 17, she became the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

Her father ran a school in Swat. When the Pakistani Taliban took control of the valley in 2008 and 2009, they banned girls from school and blew up schools. At age 11 Malala wrote a blog for the BBC's Urdu service under a pen name, describing life under their rule, and later spoke openly in the media.

On 9 October 2012 a gunman boarded her school bus and shot her. She was flown to Birmingham in England for treatment and recovered. The attack caused outrage around the world. She went on to address the United Nations, wrote the memoir I Am Malala, and set up the Malala Fund for girls' schooling. She shared the Nobel Prize with Kailash Satyarthi, an Indian campaigner against child labour. She later studied at Oxford. Her cause stands against bans such as the Afghan Taliban's bar on girls' schooling.
